prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: what is the latest competitor price check of each product in the Earbuds category? observed_ts holds UTC time. Keep exactly one check per product. When two checks of a product tie on observed_ts, the one whose competitor comes first alphabetically is kept. Return four columns, in this order: product_id, competitor, observed_ts and price_eur, from that check. Return one row for each Earbuds product with a competitor check. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check the direction of the numbering: the question asks for each product's latest check.
The row numbered 1 is the first in the window's order, so the order must put the most recent check first.
starter_sql:
WITH ranked AS (  -- one row per competitor check of an Earbuds product
  SELECT cp.product_id, cp.competitor, cp.observed_ts, cp.price_eur,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cp.product_id ORDER BY cp.observed_ts, cp.competitor) AS rn
  FROM competitor_prices cp
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = cp.product_id
  JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
  WHERE c.category_name = 'Earbuds'
)
SELECT product_id, competitor, observed_ts, price_eur
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
why_this_works: Sorting each product's checks by observed_ts with DESC puts the latest first, so rn = 1 keeps the most recent check; ascending kept the first one.
